Let \(r\) be the number of rational row labels. Then there are \(50-r\) rational column labels, so the number of rational-rational cells is

\[
r(50-r).
\]

The number of irrational-irrational cells is

\[
(50-r)r,
\]

and at most all of them can be rational. Rational-irrational cells are always irrational. Therefore the total number of rational sums is at most

\[
r(50-r)+(50-r)r=2r(50-r)\le 2\cdot 25\cdot 25=1250.
\]

This bound is achievable: take \(25\) rational rows and \(25\) rational columns. Choose the \(25\) irrational row labels as \(\sqrt2+q_i\) and the \(25\) irrational column labels as \(-\sqrt2+p_j\), with all \(q_i,p_j\) distinct rationals. Then every irrational-irrational sum is \(q_i+p_j\), hence rational. Thus we get

\[
25\cdot 25+25\cdot 25=1250
\]

rational sums.

\[
\boxed{1250}
\]
